_note: Wheat & meslin (HS 1001). Balances are USDA FAS PSD marketing-year 2024/25 (grain basis, 1,000 MT). MY2024/25 = roughly July 2024-June 2025 for Northern Hemisphere; Dec-Nov for Australia/Argentina. EU = EU-27 bloc node. Flows are bilateral trade lines: 'observed' = a published/corroborated figure (year + source in note); 'modeled' = curated route with stated basis. Many bilateral flows are stated in calendar-year customs value or volume terms where that is what the source publishes; notes make the basis explicit.

RUS.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod 81600 / cons ~47000 / exp ~44000 / imp ~250 kt. World's #1 wheat exporter (~22% of global trade).

EU.note: USDA PSD EU-27 MY2024/25: prod ~121800 / cons ~105000 / exp ~32000 (incl durum) / imp ~11000 kt. Soft-wheat exports fell ~35% on the poor French 2024 crop; France, Romania, Germany, Bulgaria, Lithuania are the main exporting members.

USA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod 53600 / cons ~30500 / exp ~22000 / imp ~3400 kt. Exports rebounded on competitive pricing; ~826 mn bushels shipped.

CAN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~34900 / cons ~9300 / exp ~26500 / imp ~500 kt. Canada was on track to be the world's 3rd-largest exporter in 2024/25 (CGC/USDA).

AUS.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25 (Oct-Sep): prod ~34100 / cons ~8500 / exp ~23500 kt. Australian Grains Industry reported 23.5 Mt shipped in MY2024/25.

UKR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~22000 / cons ~6000 / exp ~16000 kt. Black Sea corridor restored most export capacity despite war disruption.

ARG.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25 (Dec-Nov): prod ~17500 / cons ~6500 / exp ~12000 kt. USDA later forecast a record ~19.5 Mt as the new crop came in; Brazil is the dominant destination.

KAZ.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~18000 / cons ~7000 / exp ~12000 kt. Supplies flour & grain across Central Asia (Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan) plus China.

CHN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~140100 (world's largest) / cons ~149000 / imp ~8000 kt. Imports cut sharply from the ~13 Mt 2023/24 peak as domestic stocks were drawn down.

IND.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~113300 (2nd-largest) / cons ~111000 kt. Exports remained banned/restricted since May 2022 to protect domestic supply.

PAK.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~28200 / cons ~30500 / imp ~1000 kt. Large producer that still imports in deficit years.

TUR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~19000 / cons ~19500 / exp ~5500 (flour/re-export) / imp ~6500 kt. A mid-2024 import suspension to defend domestic prices cut purchases sharply.

EGY.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~9500 / cons ~21500 / imp ~12500 kt. One of the two largest wheat importers; ~75-80% sourced from Russia.

IDN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: no domestic wheat; cons ~11500 / imp ~12000 kt (flour re-export ~600). Tied with Egypt as the world's largest wheat importer.

DZA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~3000 / cons ~11000 / imp ~8500 kt. OAIC tenders source mainly from the EU (France) and Black Sea.

BRA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~8100 / cons ~12800 / imp ~6500 kt. Argentina is the dominant supplier via Mercosur; import value up ~27% in 2024.

NGA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: cons ~5800 / imp ~5500 kt. Top sub-Saharan importer; EU (incl Lithuania/Latvia/Poland) and Russia/US are main suppliers.

MAR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~2500 (drought-hit) / cons ~10500 / imp ~7500 kt. France and Black Sea origins dominate.

BGD.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~1200 / cons ~8200 / imp ~7000 kt. Russia, then Canada/Ukraine/India(when open) supply.

PHL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: cons ~7300 / imp ~7000 kt. US and Australia are the dominant milling-wheat suppliers; feed wheat from Black Sea.

JPN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~1000 / cons ~6400 / imp ~5500 kt. MAFF tenders source US, Canada, Australia in fixed shares.

KOR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: cons ~4200 / imp ~4200 kt. US, Australia, Canada supply milling & feed wheat.

MEX.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~3000 / cons ~8000 / imp ~5800 kt. US is the overwhelming supplier (NAFTA/USMCA proximity).

DEU.note: Eurostat/USDA MY2024/25: prod ~18000 / exp ~5500 / imp ~4500 kt. Large EU producer; both an intra-EU trader and importer of milling wheat.

FRA.note: USDA/FranceAgriMer MY2024/25: prod ~25500 (down ~25% on a wet 2024 harvest) / exp ~9500 kt. The EU's leading wheat exporter even in a weak year.

ROU.note: USDA MY2024/25: prod ~9500 / exp ~5000 kt. Constanta port is a key Black Sea outlet for Romanian and transiting Ukrainian wheat.

GBR.note: AHDB/USDA MY2024/25: prod ~11100 (down on a wet 2024) / imp ~3000 kt. Net importer in poor harvest years.

SAU.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: cons ~4000 / imp ~3500 kt. SAGO tenders source EU, Black Sea, Australia, Canada.

ITA.note: USDA/ITC MY2024/25: prod ~6800 / imp ~5500 kt. Large durum & milling importer; Russia, Romania, Ukraine, France, Canada supply.

ESP.note: USDA/ITC MY2024/25: prod ~7000 / imp ~6500 kt. Large feed-wheat importer; sources Black Sea, France, UK, Argentina.

ZAF.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~2100 / cons ~3700 / imp ~1900 kt. Sources from Russia, Australia, Argentina, EU; re-exports to neighbours.

UZB.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~6200 / imp ~2500 kt, almost entirely from Kazakhstan and Russia overland.

VNM.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: cons ~5200 / imp ~5000 kt. Australia and Black Sea origins supply milling & feed wheat.

KEN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~2300 kt. Russia, Ukraine, Argentina, Australia supply.

THA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~3700 kt (feed + milling). Australia, Black Sea, India(when open) supply.

COL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~2100 kt. US, Canada, Argentina supply milling wheat.

TWN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~1300 kt, mostly US milling wheat under purchasing agreements.

PER.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~2000 kt. Canada, US, Argentina supply.

MYS.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~1900 kt, mostly Australian milling wheat; some flour re-export.

CHL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~1300 / imp ~1100 kt, mainly from Argentina.

AFG.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~4500 / imp ~2000 kt (wheat + flour), mostly overland from Kazakhstan.

TJK.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imp ~1000 kt, supplied overland by Kazakhstan.

rankings.note: Export/import values are 1,000 MT (grain basis) from USDA FAS PSD for marketing year 2024/25. Russia leads world exports (~22% share); Egypt and Indonesia are the two largest importers (~12.5 Mt each). EU shown as a bloc; intra-EU trade excluded from the bloc figure.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$160-177bn (FY2024); privately held, one of the largest grain traders.
companies.note: Member of the 'ABCD' majors that handle the bulk of internationally traded grain. Global origination across North & South America, Black Sea and the EU; large port and elevator network.
companies.improve: Cargill is privately held and discloses little segment-level wheat volume or origin detail. Publishing audited per-origin tonnage and Black Sea exposure would let buyers and analysts size concentration risk rather than infer it.

companies.name: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM)
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$85bn (FY2024); Ag Services & Oilseeds is the core grain-handling segment.
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD' majors. Large North American and Black Sea origination, milling and logistics footprint.
companies.improve: ADM should break out wheat (vs. corn/soy) origination volumes by region and disclose Black Sea sourcing exposure, which is currently bundled inside Ag Services.

companies.name: Bunge Global (Bunge–Viterra)
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$53bn (Bunge FY2024); the ~US$34bn Bunge–Viterra merger completed July 2025 created a top-tier grain trader.
companies.note: Post-merger Bunge-Viterra is one of the largest global grain handlers, with deep Canadian (Viterra Prairie elevators), Australian and Black Sea origination added to Bunge's Americas base.
companies.improve: Integration of Viterra's Canadian/Australian assets concentrates a large share of Prairie and Black Sea wheat handling in one firm; transparent post-merger origin-share reporting would address competition and concentration concerns.

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$50bn (FY2024); the 'D' in ABCD, with a Grains & Oilseeds platform.
companies.note: Major Black Sea, South American and EU wheat originator; acquired Viterra divestiture assets in the EU as a remedy to the Bunge-Viterra merger.
companies.improve: Privately held; LDC discloses limited per-commodity origin data. Region-level wheat tonnage disclosure would improve traceability of its Black Sea and South American flows.

companies.name: COFCO International
companies.metric: Agribusiness revenue rivals the ABCD majors; China's state-linked global grain trader.
companies.note: COFCO is the leading channel for grain into China and a top-5 global trader, with strong Black Sea and South American origination.
companies.improve: State linkage and limited Western disclosure make COFCO's wheat origination opaque; published origin-share data would clarify its role in China's import security.

companies.name: Viterra (now part of Bunge)
companies.metric: Largest grain handler on the Canadian Prairies and a major Australian originator; merged into Bunge (July 2025).
companies.note: Historically the dominant Western Canadian wheat collector (ex-Glencore Agriculture); its elevator and port network underpins Canada's #3 export position.
companies.improve: As the Canadian-Prairie wheat handling consolidates under Bunge, antitrust remedies and transparent Prairie origin-share reporting matter for grower pricing power.

global.note: World wheat totals, 1,000 MT (grain basis), USDA FAS PSD. MY2024/25 production a record ~793.8 Mt; world exports ~209 Mt; consumption ~803.7 Mt. Years labelled by the start of the marketing year.

forecast.method: Projected 2030 value = 2024 value × (1 + CAGR)^6, per metric. Net = projected production − projected consumption. CAGR figures are reasoned assumptions inside the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2024-2033 envelope (global wheat demand +~12% by 2033, output rising mainly via yield) and USDA long-term projections — stated openly so they can be challenged.

scenarios.label: Black Sea export disruption (Russia + Ukraine ports)
scenarios.note: Russia (~44 Mt) and Ukraine (~16 Mt) together supply ~30% of world wheat trade. A renewed corridor breakdown, port strike or escalation could cut Black Sea exportable supply ~30-40%, hitting Egypt, Turkey, Bangladesh and sub-Saharan importers hardest (USDA/IGC).

scenarios.label: Russia tightens wheat export quota/tax 25%
scenarios.note: Russia routinely uses export quotas and floating duties to manage domestic prices; a tightening of ~25% would squeeze its biggest customers Egypt (8 Mt) and Turkey, forcing them toward pricier EU/US origins (Rusagrotrans/USDA).

scenarios.label: Australian drought cuts exports 25%
scenarios.note: Australian wheat output swings widely with ENSO; an El Niño drought can cut the ~23.5 Mt export program 20-30%, raising prices for Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam that depend on Australian milling wheat (USDA/ABARES).

scenarios.label: India keeps export ban / global tightness
scenarios.note: India is the #2 producer (~113 Mt) but has banned exports since May 2022. A continued ban plus a poor monsoon keeps ~10 Mt of potential supply off the market and could even turn India into an importer, tightening Asian balances (USDA).

scenarios.label: EU wet-weather harvest failure (France-led)
scenarios.note: The wet 2024 French harvest already cut EU soft-wheat exports ~35%. A repeat would remove milling wheat that Morocco, Algeria and Nigeria rely on, pushing them onto Black Sea and forcing quality substitution (EU Commission/USDA).

scenarios.label: Argentina reimposes wheat export taxes 30%
scenarios.note: Argentina has repeatedly used export taxes (retenciones) to curb domestic food prices; a 30% disincentive would cut shipments to Brazil — which takes ~6 Mt via tariff-free Mercosur — and push Brazil toward US/Black Sea wheat at higher cost (USDA/ITC).
